verdicts.title: Contributor documentation routes public users to GitHub Discussions (disabled) and to label URLs that do not match the repository's actual label names
verdicts.reasoning: Every link in the evidence chain re-verified against the current tree and the live GitHub API. (1) CONTRIBUTING.md:87 '- [Open Discussions](https://github.com/JetBrains-Research/opaque/discussions)' and CONTRIBUTING.md:445 '- **Questions**: Open a [Discussion](.../discussions)' are present at exactly those lines. GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque returns has_discussions: false, private: false, visibility: public, so both URLs point at a feature that is off. Issue #566 ('docs: configure GitHub Discussions for public participation', milestone Marble) is closed with state_reason 'not_planned' and closed_by_pull_requests total_count 0 — the decision not to enable Discussions was taken and the docs that #566 would have made valid were never reverted. (2) CONTRIBUTING.md:85-86 link /labels/good-first-issue and /labels/help-wanted. GET /repos/.../labels/good-first-issue and /labels/help-wanted both return 'label not found'; GET /labels/good%20first%20issue returns {name: 'good first issue', color 7057ff} and /labels/help%20wanted returns {name: 'help wanted', color 008672}. The hyphenated slugs in the docs correspond to no label in the repository. (3) ls .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ shows only bug_report.yml, documentation.yml, feature_request.yml — no config.yml, so the new-issue chooser carries no contact_links. One correction that reduces impact: list_issues with labels ['good first issue'] and ['help wanted'] both return totalCount 0, so even the correctly-encoded links would list nothing today; the slug bug turns an empty filter into a non-existent one. I could not independently fetch the HTTP status of the label/discussions pages (the outbound proxy returns 403 for github.com HTML), so the '404 vs empty page' detail rests on GitHub's documented routing rather than my own fetch; the underlying facts (feature off, labels do not exist, no config.yml) are API-verified. This is a documentation/community-health defect with no code, privacy, or epsilon impact, so low is the right severity.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A first-time contributor following CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Good starting points' clicks /labels/good-first-issue and /labels/help-wanted; neither slug exists in the repository (the real labels are 'good first issue' and 'help wanted', and today both carry zero issues), so neither link surfaces a startable task. The 'Open Discussions' link at CONTRIBUTING.md:87 and the sole 'Questions' route at CONTRIBUTING.md:445 both target github.com/.../discussions, but has_discussions is false (issue #566 was closed not_planned), so neither resolves. With no .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml the new-issue chooser offers no contact links either, leaving the public issue tracker as the only working channel — discoverable, but not the one the documentation names. Three dead links in the contributor entry point; no code, privacy, or epsilon consequence.

verdicts.title: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is disabled on the public repository and SECURITY.md states no concrete disclosure window
verdicts.reasoning: Both factual halves reproduced. GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque/private-vulnerability-reporting returns HTTP 200 {"enabled": false}, and the repo is public (private: false, visibility: 'public'), so the GitHub-native 'Report a vulnerability' form is indeed unavailable. SECURITY.md re-read in full (51 lines): lines 11-15 direct reporters to security@jetbrains.com with a PGP key and forbid public issues/discussions; lines 39-43 delegate handling to the JetBrains Coordinated Disclosure Policy and say only 'Please allow reasonable time for a fix or mitigation before public disclosure'. grep confirms no number of days anywhere in the file. Two corrections that materially soften the finding as written. First, the framed consequence is overstated: SECURITY.md exists at the repository root, which is exactly what GitHub renders as 'Security policy' on the Security tab and in the repo sidebar, so a researcher does see a designated private route (the mailto plus PGP key) — the missing item is the native form, not the private channel. Second, SECURITY.md:28-35 already routes non-sensitive DP/accounting defects to the public tracker and reserves the private channel for material-privacy-impact cases, so the 'no visible correct destination' framing does not hold. Delegating the timeline to a real, reachable org-level coordinated-disclosure policy is a legitimate practice, not a defect; the absence of a project-specific number of days is a completeness preference. Net: two verified configuration/policy observations, no functional or privacy impact — low.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Private vulnerability reporting is toggled off on this public repository (API: {"enabled": false}), so the Security tab shows the rendered SECURITY.md policy but no native 'Report a vulnerability' draft-advisory form. An outside researcher's private route is therefore the security@jetbrains.com mailto at SECURITY.md:11-13 (with the PGP key) — a working channel, just not the 2026-standard in-product one, and its absence also means no draft GitHub Security Advisory / CVE workflow for the published opaque-* distributions. Separately, SECURITY.md states no project-specific acknowledgement or disclosure window, deferring entirely to the JetBrains Coordinated Disclosure Policy (verified reachable), so reporter and maintainer share no explicit numeric expectation. Neither item causes a wrong result or a privacy loss.

verdicts.title: Removing the contract tests (#586) left the documented torch-free opaque-accounting guarantee with no automated enforcement, in the repository or post-build
verdicts.reasoning: Verified end to end. git show 864a6442 --stat (delete(contracts): replace fragile checks with Junie review (#587), 2026-08-14) deletes tests/contracts/test_accounting_torch_free.py (55 lines) and tests/contracts/test_accounting_factory_leakage.py (89 lines) plus eight other enumeration/import tests; tests/ now contains only _support/ and integration/ — no contracts/ directory. Nothing replaced the torch-free guard: grep -rn -i 'torch.free' over the tree returns only prose (packages/opaque-base/pyproject.toml:26,30; two module docstrings; packages/opaque-base/README.md:17; README.md:42; AGENTS.md:32,41,127,130) and one orphaned section header at packages/opaque-auditing/tests/auditing/test_eps_delta.py:161 ('# ---- Contract: torch-free ---') whose body the same commit deleted — a dangling comment with no assertion under it. .github/workflows/validate-distributions.yml (81 lines total; the only artifact-validation workflow) has exactly one job, install-all, which installs "${opaque_wheels[0]}[all]" and runs a cross-stack DP-SGD|DP-FTRL composition; there is no opaque-accounting-only or torch-free install path anywhere in it. The property still holds today: grep -rn 'torch' packages/opaque-accounting/ matches only a docstring mention in _process_codec.py:6, and packages/opaque-accounting/pyproject.toml dependencies = ['opaque-base>=0.0.0.dev0']. So this is an unguarded documented invariant, not a live break — exactly as the finding states. One fairness note the finding already acknowledges: .junie/architecture-contracts.md marks ARC-004, ARC-005 and ARC-011 'Planned' and instructs reviewers not to report absent planned infrastructure as a violation, so the gap is a consciously deferred one rather than an oversight. Low severity: a test-coverage gap on a packaging guarantee, no current defect, no epsilon impact.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: No test or CI job currently asserts that opaque-accounting imports without torch, although README.md:42, AGENTS.md:32/41/130 and the installation docs advertise 'pip install opaque-accounting' as torch-free standalone. The two contract tests that enforced it were deleted in 864a6442 (#587) and the sole post-build scenario in .github/workflows/validate-distributions.yml installs opaque[all], where torch is always present. A future change that adds an 'import torch' (directly or through an opaque-engine helper) under packages/opaque-accounting/src would pass every lane, and the published wheel — which declares only opaque-base — would fail to import in the environment the docs promise. The property is verified to hold at 12146ec4 (no torch import under packages/opaque-accounting), so this is a missing guard, not a break; the replacement post-build validation (ARC-004/ARC-005/ARC-011) is explicitly marked 'Planned' in .junie/architecture-contracts.md.

verdicts.title: A 60 KB internal research diary sits at the public repository root, unreferenced by any documentation and carrying stale claims about defects
verdicts.reasoning: Every element reproduced. issue-795-research.md is a tracked root-level file, 60100 bytes / 1064 lines, sitting directly beside README.md, LICENSE, NOTICE and SECURITY.md in `ls` of the repo root. git log --oneline -- issue-795-research.md returns exactly one commit, d09d7b9a 'fix(dpftrl): bound BISR noise state by bandwidth (#886)'. It is orphaned: grep -rn 'issue-795' over *.md/*.yml/*.toml/*.py excluding the file itself returns nothing, and mkdocs.yml does not mention it. Its content is a working diary — line 1-3 '# Issue 795: bounded-memory BISR noise execution / Research snapshot: 2026-08-31 UTC', line 5 '## Post-research implementation update (2026-09-01 UTC)', followed by rebase provenance (naming e64846c9, PR #857, e87a0c21), superseded recommendations and running commentary on other issues — precisely what AGENTS.md's Documentation section tells contributors to keep out of the tree ('Keep user-facing docs and code comments diary-free ... Migration narrative belongs in PR bodies and the changelog'). The staleness is real: lines 45-47 call issue #789 'the separate, urgent calibrated-resume defect', line 979 says 'The calibrated-resume failure in #789 remains urgent', and line 1014 repeats 'the urgent enforcement gap is #789'; GET /repos/.../issues/789 returns state 'closed', state_reason 'completed', closed_at 2026-09-04T07:49:39Z, closed_by evgri243 (title: 'Stop calibrated DP-FTRL resume from silently changing sigma mid-horizon', labels include 'impact: epsilon'). So a public root-level file asserts an unfixed epsilon-affecting defect that was fixed nine days before the audited commit. Not tracked by any open issue in the milestone or non-milestone open lists. Low severity: public-messaging and repo-hygiene only, no code, test, or privacy effect.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: issue-795-research.md (60100 bytes, 1064 lines) is committed at the public repository root next to README.md and LICENSE, introduced by d09d7b9a and referenced by nothing — not mkdocs.yml, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, or docs/. It reads as an internal engineering memo (rebase provenance, superseded recommendations, commentary on other issues), which AGENTS.md's documentation rule excludes from the tree, and it is already stale in a way that misstates the project: lines 45-47, 979 and 1014 describe issue #789 — an epsilon-affecting calibrated-resume defect — as 'urgent' and unfixed, while #789 was closed as completed on 2026-09-04. A prospective user or reviewer browsing the repository root reads that the library has an outstanding urgent privacy-calibration defect when it does not. Nothing builds, links, or tests the file, so it will keep drifting.
